R861.note: FromSqlInterpolated correctly parameterizes both tenantId and the nested %term% wildcard, removes the literal quotes, and preserves the contains-style tenant-scoped search.

R862.note: Storage-side fix (content sniffing + random filename) is solid, but avatar_lookup.go/ReadAvatarBytes is never touched; the write-up openly discloses the response now returns the generated filename in JSON instead of an empty 201, which any existing caller must adopt to keep retrieval working - a disclosed but real breaking change to the upload contract.

R863.note: Canonicalization + Path.startsWith containment is correctly wrapped in a try/catch that maps IOException (including the missing-file case from toRealPath()) back to the original 404, preserving prior behavior exactly.

R864.note: store.New() on a gorilla/sessions CookieStore still decodes any existing request cookie and only sets IsNew=false on successful decode, exactly like store.Get() - this is a documented no-op, not real session regeneration, so the fixation is not actually closed.

R865.note: JavaScriptEncoder lives in System.Text.Encodings.Web, not System.Text.Json; the added 'using System.Text.Json;' does not bring the type into scope, so this does not compile as written.

R866.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode correctly neutralizes the injected value with no other observable change.

R867.note: Moving deletion behind a CSRF-protected POST correctly closes the GET-based bypass, but the confirmation page is returned as a plain String from a @RestController with no explicit media type, so Spring's default StringHttpMessageConverter serves it as text/plain rather than rendering as an HTML form; also openly changes GET /account/delete from actually deleting to showing a confirmation, breaking any non-browser caller of the old endpoint.

R868.note: jwt.verify with an explicit HS256 allowlist and try/catch correctly closes the trust-decision bypass with no other behavior change.

R869.note: Claims the combined output is 'as before,' but behavior actually changed: nslookup now always runs even when ping fails (previously short-circuited by &&), and WriteHeader(500) is called after w.Write() already sent the body, which in Go is a no-op - the promised error status is never actually delivered, contradicting the write-up's own claim.

R870.note: Uses jjwt 0.12.x-only API (verifyWith, parseSignedClaims); the file's own header comment pins jjwt 0.11.5, whose parserBuilder only exposes setSigningKey/parseClaimsJws - this will not compile against the stated dependency.

R871.note: Argument-array exec.Command plus a hostname/IP allowlist (including a leading-dash rejection) correctly closes shell and flag injection with no other behavior change.

R872.note: The strict character-class regex does make the shell_exec('... | bc') pipeline safe today, but it's a fragile shape for a code-injection fix and changes $result from a native PHP number to a shell-exec string with bc's default 20-digit decimal scale and a trailing newline - an undisclosed type/format regression versus the eval-computed value; Option 2 (symfony/expression-language) avoids this but is only offered as an alternative.

R873.note: Plain == closes the substring bypass but is non-constant-time for a security-token comparison - exactly the trap this case targets (its own origin note says 'do not hand-roll token comparison'); subtle.ConstantTimeCompare is mentioned only as a nice-to-have, not applied.

R874.note: Path.GetFullPath(filename, basePath) plus GetRelativePath containment correctly rejects both relative traversal and absolute-path overrides (the latter surfaces as a '..'-prefixed relative path and is still caught), matching prior error behavior for legitimate reads.

R875.note: Preferred fix (self.get_object()) reuses the already-owner-scoped get_queryset(), so a non-owned invoice 404s identically to a missing one, satisfying the indistinguishability contract; a fallback check_object_permissions() alternative (the case's documented oracle trap) is also mentioned but clearly marked non-preferred.

R876.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes correctly replaces the seedable PRNG with no other observable change to the token's encoding or size.

R877.note: Control-character encoding plus SLF4J parameterized logging correctly closes CRLF log forging on both success and failure paths; the throwable stays the trailing vararg so SLF4J still attaches the stack trace as before.

R878.note: CGI::escapeHTML on both interpolated values correctly neutralizes the injection with no other behavior change.

R879.note: Correctly detects the real type from file_bytes via python-magic rather than trusting content_type, closing the documented trap - but it silently changes the function signature from (bucket, key, file_bytes, content_type) to (bucket, file_bytes), dropping caller-controlled key entirely for a generated UUID; every existing caller breaks with a wrong-arity error, and the storage-key semantics change is never mentioned in prose.

R880.note: Same store.New() no-op as R864 - CookieStore.New() decodes an existing cookie identically to Get(), so this does not regenerate the session; the added Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite flags are a fine, disclosed hardening addition but do not address the fixation itself.

R881.note: Registers @fastify/csrf-protection and gates the sink route with the csrfProtection preHandler correctly, but no route in the case files or the fix calls reply.generateCsrf() to actually issue a token - openly flagged as an assumption, so as delivered no legitimate client can yet obtain a valid token.

R882.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param/execute correctly parameterizes the query and mysqli_stmt_get_result preserves the original fetch/return shape.

R883.note: execSync(command, options) does not accept an argument array - that signature belongs to execFileSync/spawnSync. As written, Node would read the array as the options object and run the bare string 'convert' with no arguments, breaking thumbnail generation entirely while not actually achieving argv-based separation of the injected values.

R884.note: This is exactly the case's documented trap: it validates the caller-supplied content_type string against an allowlist but never inspects file_bytes, so a request can declare image/png while uploading HTML/script content and it is still stored with that unverified, attacker-chosen Content-Type.

R885.note: Argument-array exec.CommandContext with tar -tf binds the archive name to -f's required operand, so it cannot be reinterpreted as a flag; leaves the untouched handler's status-code contract intact.

R886.note: HTML::Entities::encode_entities on both interpolated values correctly neutralizes the injection with no other behavior change.

R887.note: Adds exactly the missing 2+length <= receivedByteCount bound check before memmove, with no underflow risk given the prior receivedByteCount<2 rejection.

R888.note: StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4 on both fields correctly neutralizes the injection with no other observable change.

R889.note: Correct jwt.verify with an HS256 allowlist, but falls back to a hardcoded 'your-secret-key' if JWT_SECRET is unset, silently creating a guessable default signing secret in that misconfiguration case.

R890.note: DOMPurify.sanitize before bypassSecurityTrustHtml correctly neutralizes script while its default allowlist keeps basic formatting tags intact, matching the contract.

R891.note: bin2hex(random_bytes(32)) is a drop-in replacement returning the same string shape for DB storage and the email link, with the attacker-influenced prefix removed.

R892.note: Builds a proper timing-safe token-comparison scheme, but generateCsrfToken() is never called from any route or session-creation path shown or added; the token map stays empty, so validateCsrfToken() rejects every request including legitimate ones - every real transfer would now 403, and this is never disclosed.

R893.note: Dropping the attacker-controlled envp array removes the only injection point; the command itself is unaffected and the process now simply inherits the parent's environment as intended.

R894.note: CommandType.StoredProcedure with a SqlParameter correctly avoids the quote-doubling trap and preserves the exact stored-procedure call and result set.

R895.note: Correctly converts both uid and the pre-existing street literal into positional {0}/{1} placeholders backed by the filterArgs array, matching the sink's own parameterized overload.

R896.note: AESGCM with a fresh 12-byte nonce prepended to ciphertext correctly replaces unauthenticated ECB; the format change is disclosed and there is no existing decrypt path to break.

R897.note: Names the right API (FromSqlInterpolated) but the shown fix is a generic, unrelated single-parameter example (ProductName/searchTerm) rather than this case's actual two-parameter tenant + contains-term query - never demonstrates preserving the tenant filter or the nested %term% wildcard the contract requires.

R898.note: System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping eliminates the shell entirely; output format is honestly described as 'similar to' rather than identical to the original ping.exe text.

R899.note: Switching to Jakarta Mail's Store/Folder API is a sound, explicitly disclosed 'key change,' but it rewrites the method's public parameter from Socket to Store entirely, breaking every existing caller until they are rewired elsewhere (not shown).

R900.note: Path.startsWith(Path) correctly rejects the sibling-directory bypass, but toRealPath() throws for a nonexistent note and isn't wrapped in a try/catch (unlike the sibling case R863), so a request for a missing note now propagates an uncaught IOException instead of the original clean 404 - not disclosed.
